function: p. 2-3: CSI feedback: GLCsiNet encoder compresses the angular-delay CSI matrix at the UE into an M-dimensional vector and the decoder reconstructs it at the BS.
system: p. 2, 4: FDD downlink, BS with Nt=32 antennas, UE with one receive antenna, Nc=1024 subcarriers; 5.3 GHz indoor and 300 MHz outdoor COST 2100 scenarios; no RIS.
method: p. 3-4: Autoencoder with GRU (global features) and DSConv plus FasterNet (local features), trained supervised to reconstruct the CSI matrix; cosine annealing, 1000 epochs, dropout.
data_channel: p. 4: Two scenarios generated using the publicly available COST 2100 dataset: 5.3 GHz indoor and 300 MHz outdoor rural; 100,000 training, 30,000 validation, 20,000 test CSI matrices.
test_conditions: p. 4: Indoor and outdoor scenarios reported separately, compression ratios 1/4 to 1/64; training, validation, and test sets of 100,000, 30,000, and 20,000 matrices; no cross-scenario test reported.
baselines: p. 4-5: Learned CsiNet [2], CsiNet+ [4], TransNet [9], DDCsiNet [10] (Table I, p. 5); no non-learned method compared.
metrics: p. 4-5: NMSE in dB of the reconstructed CSI matrix at five compression ratios; FLOPs in millions (Table I); NMSE and FLOPs versus feature-sequence size (Fig. 7).
complexity: p. 5: Table I: GLCsiNet FLOPs from 16.2 M (gamma=1/4) to 10.83 M (1/64), versus 325.2 M for DDCsiNet and 33.75-35.72 M for TransNet; FLOPs only, no runtime.
openness: none; no code or data link (the public COST 2100 dataset, p. 4, ref. [16], is used)
q1_support: p. 4: "generated using the publicly available COST 2100 [16] dataset", with a 5.3 GHz indoor and a 300 MHz outdoor rural scenario.
q2_support: p. 4: "The training, validation, and testing sets consist of 100,000, 30,000, and 20,000 CSI matrices, respectively", a split of the same data; indoor and outdoor are reported separately (Table I, p. 5) and no model trained on one scenario is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 4: "a comprehensive comparison of GLCsiNet with several representative DL-based methods"; Table I (p. 5) lists only CsiNet, CsiNet+, TransNet, and DDCsiNet, and "traditional methods [3]" appear only on p. 1, so no non-learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "GLCsiNet holds a significant advantage by requiring only 3.9% of the FLOPs used by DDCsiNet"; Table I lists FLOPs (M) per model and p. 4 derives the FLOPs of DSConv versus normal convolution.
q5_support: p. 4: "the publicly available COST 2100 [16] dataset" is used for training and testing; no link or DOI to the generated data or to code is given.
notes: Included, area 2: the learned function is CSI feedback (compression and reconstruction of the CSI matrix). The UE has one receive antenna but the BS has 32, so the system check passes. q3 is 0 because Table I compares only learned methods; the reviewer can check the table on p. 5. q1 and q5 rest on the paper calling COST 2100 a publicly available dataset (p. 4); it also says it generated the two scenarios itself and gives no link, so the reviewer may want to confirm q5.
